title: Browser automation without code: tools and limits | 50agents
description: No-code browser automation comes in three kinds: recorders, scrapers and AI browser agents. What each is good at, where each breaks, and how to start.
answer: There are three kinds: recorders that replay your clicks, scrapers that pull data from pages, and AI browser agents that read a page and decide.
Pick by the job: many similar pages, stable clicks, or pages that change.

root.q: What does the job do on the website?

options.label: Pulls the same data from pages

then.why: You point it at the data on one page and it pulls the same fields from every similar page. It breaks when the layout changes, so spot-check it.
It reads each page from your description, so a moved button or a new layout does not stop it. It can misjudge an ambiguous page.

then.q: Does the site stay the same?

then.why: Click through once while it records, and it replays the same clicks as often as you like. A pop-up or a moved button breaks it.
Describe the job in words; it reads the page before it clicks, and asks you before it signs in or submits anything.
Reading, comparing and deciding what matters is the part recorders and scrapers cannot do.

body.p: Check two things in any plan: whether failed runs are billed (Axiom does not count them against its runtime), and whether runs happen in the cloud or need your computer awake. For how the units become a bill, see [how much automation costs](/guides/how-much-automation-costs-credits-tasks-and-runs-compared).

method.h2: How to automate a browser without code, step by step

steps.title: Write the job as clicks
steps.body: Which site, which pages, what to read or fill, and how often. Count the pages per run.

steps.title: Pick the kind
steps.body: Many pages with the same layout: a scraper. The same clicks daily on a stable tool: a recorder. A few pages that move or need reading: a browser agent.

steps.title: Check cloud or desktop
steps.body: If it must run at 6:00 while your laptop sleeps, you need cloud runs.

note.text: A desktop-only tool misses every scheduled run while your computer is asleep or off.

steps.title: Plan the sign-in
steps.body: Sites behind a login need a kept session. Avoid tools that want your password stored in a text field.

steps.title: Run it for a week, checking each run
steps.body: Each run should end with a check: a count, a confirmation, a file. Look at every run that first week.

captain.line: Captain sets up a browser agent with its own browser, on a schedule. It shows the page live while it works and lists the pages it visited in each report.
captain.ask: Set up a browser agent that reads the new listings on rentals.example each morning and tells me the ones under $2,000 in Riverside

wrong.title: "No code" turns into code
wrong.body: Users of several tools report needing custom scripts past the basics. Try your hardest page in the free tier before you commit.

wrong.title: Credits burned on failures
wrong.body: A broken page gets retried all night. Check how failed runs are billed, and cap retries.

wrong.title: Quietly wrong data
wrong.body: A scraper picks the wrong column after a redesign. Spot-check a few values each week.

faqs.q: Is there a free browser automation tool?
faqs.a: UI.Vision is open source and free. Browse AI and Bardeen have free tiers with small monthly limits; Axiom gives a short free runtime to try.

faqs.q: Can browser automation run on a schedule?
faqs.a: Yes, on cloud plans. Desktop tools run only while your computer is on and awake.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a browser agent and a scraper?
faqs.a: A scraper pulls the same fields from pages you trained it on. A browser agent reads the page and decides what to do from your description, so it handles pages it has not seen, and can also misjudge them.
